Arsenal midfielder Martin Zubimendi has dismissed reports linking him with a possible departure from the club, insisting that he is happy in North London and focused on competing for playing time. The Spanish international addressed the speculation in an interview with Spanish newspaper Marca on Wednesday, expressing surprise at reports suggesting he could leave Arsenal as the January transfer window approaches. Zubimendi said media organisations needed to exercise caution when reporting transfer rumours, stressing that every player had a responsibility to respect their current club. “I’m sometimes surprised by the press. I understand the transfer window is approaching, but I think we need to be a bit more careful with what we publish,” he said. The midfielder explained that Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta had discussed the club’s plans with him before the beginning of the season, making it clear that competition for places would increase following the arrival of new players. And here we are, fighting for it.” The 27-year-old acknowledged the quality within Arsenal’s squad, noting that competition for regular playing time was expected at a club featuring several top-level footballers. There are some fantastic players … I’m calm and happy,” he added. Zubimendi joined Arsenal from Spanish side Real Sociedad in the summer of 2025 after establishing himself as one of the prominent midfielders in European football. His arrival strengthened Arteta’s midfield options as the club continued its pursuit of major domestic and European honours. The midfielder’s latest comments appear to dismiss speculation surrounding his future, with the Spaniard indicating that he remains comfortable with Arsenal’s plans and is prepared to compete for his place in the team. His immediate focus remains on contributing to Arteta’s squad rather than considering an exit from the Emirates Stadium.
